title: Cohort Bridge Patterns for LLM A/B Orchestration (WIP)
body:
Purpose
This is a working sketch for a cross-functional pattern were calling "cohort bridge" — a set of operational contracts and traffic choreography primitives intended to safely ramp LLM changes across heterogenous deployments (hosted, dedicated, private) and across user cohorts with differing risk profiles.

Notes and motivation
- Problem: canonical canary slices often assume homogenous infra and identical SLOs. With Redwoods multi-mode inference (hosted, Dedicated, Private) we need a traffic choreography that explicitly accounts for: model variant compatibility, quantized vs fp16 execution artifacts, and customer/legal constraints.
- Goal: define small, repeatable playbooks to move from 0% -> 100% exposure while minimizing blast radius and preserving rollback speed.
- Key idea: bridge small, controlled "bridge cohorts" that are both technically and behaviorally representative of the next larger slice before increasing exposure.

Glossary (short)
- Bridge cohort: a tiny cohort (0.05% - 0.5%) selected to be a microcosm of target population (mix of device types, regions, plans).
- ORCA-slice: operationally resilient cohort allocation that can be fast-reverted and has dedicated monitoring hooks (we use this name in our experiments).
- Stability leash: temporal safety limit (e.g., 2h median latency + 3x p95 deviation) where we require manual ack to continue ramp.
- Cohort bridge transition: a discrete step where traffic and routing policies change but can be programmatically reversed.

High-level pattern
1) Hypothesis and metrics
   - Short hypothesis template: "Replace model A -> model B for chat completion. Expect NLU precision delta <= 0.5% and latency change <= 15ms."
   - Primary metrics: user-visible success (task completion / click-through), degrade signals (hallucination rate proxies), token-level cost, latency p50/p95/p99, error-rate, fallback fraction (e.g., rate of reroutes to stable model).

2) Cohort selection rules (bridge cohorts)
   - Choose 2 orthogonal axes: footprint and sensitivity. Example: footprint axis = request size distribution; sensitivity axis = account tier (free vs paid).
   - Bridge cohort should contain at least 2 accounts in each of top 3 geo regions; must include at least one high-throughput API key (dedicated) and one private deployment customer (if available) to exercise routing.
   - If private deployment customers exist and are in-scope for the feature, engage solutions-engineering and get explicit signoff.

3) Deployment topology and routing
   - Deploy model B to a canary pool in hosted and dedicated infra (single GPU pool for isolation).
   - Configure smart routing rules: prefer hosted for low-latency ORCA requests with fallback to dedicated if token budget or compute mismatch.
   - Use request tagging: add header X-RW-Bridge: <bridge-id> to ensure observability and to enable fast traffic slice filtering in tracing backends.

4) Ramp recipe (suggested cadence)
   - Step 0 (dry-run): run shadow traffic for 24h for both normal and long-tail prompts; collect logits/tokens for offline evals.
   - Step 1 (ORCA-slice, 0.05%): route tiny slice to model B for 1h. Stability leash checks run at t=30m and t=1h.
   - Step 2 (bridge cohort, 0.2%): expand to microcohort for 3h if leash passed.
   - Step 3 (micro-regional ramp, 1%): expand by region where latency and error budgets are least impacted, run 6h.
   - Step 4 (broad rollout 10%): 24h observation window with automated rollback triggers enabled.
   - Step 5 (full rollout): 48h final observation then opt in for 100% traffic.
   - All steps except dry-run must be reversible via single API call and fallback policy.

5) Automated checks and abort criteria (always-on)
   - Abort if any of: error-rate > baseline + 0.5pp, p95 latency > baseline + 30%, user-visible failure signal > baseline * 1.2, fallback fraction > 5% absolute increase.
   - Soft-warning: if hallucination proxy (low-confidence NLU) increases by >10% schedule human review.

6) Observability and dashboards
   - Dedicated ORCA dashboard tile with: cohort breakdown, infra routing path, p50/p95/p99, token cost, fallback rate, per-account traces.
   - Correlate logits/confidence score drift with downstream metrics (CTR, user retention).
   - Synthetic probes: run 5 canonical prompts per minute where answers are deterministic; verify answer sketch similarity score.

7) Human gates and ownership
   - Bridge steward (product): approves each ramp step and coordinates comms.
   - Observability owner (eng/observability): ensures dashboards populated and alerts live.
   - Oncall (SRE): final authority for immediate rollback; must be paged on abort.

8) Rollback & postmortem traces
   - Rollback must restore both routing and model weights if error condition triggered.
   - Preserve traces for the ramp window and archive artifacts for offline evals.
   - Postmortem template includes: earliest anomaly time, first deviation metric, affected cohorts, rollback decision, learning actions.

Checklist (operational)
- [ ] Shadow-run logs available for 24h and sampled at token-level
- [ ] ORCA headers inserted for bridge cohorts
- [ ] Dashboards configured and smoke tests green
- [ ] Contact list (eng, product, solutions, legal if private customers) defined
- [ ] Automated abort rules created in console and verified with dry-run trigger

Experiment variants and A/B mapping guidance
- When testing product changes that include behavioral policy updates (e.g., reranker weights) run A/B with an extended leash (longer observation windows) because behavioral signal noise is higher and may need human label periods.
- For deterministic model changes (quantization only), prefer faster ramps with tightened latency leashes.

Unresolved questions / TODOs
- Need a canonical sampling library for cohort selection; current ad-hoc filters exist in analytics. Rational: minimize selection bias.
- Bridge cohorts that include private deployment customers: what consent/legal wording do we need? (Assign to legal.)
- Explore automatic cohort rotation: after 6 ramps, a cohort becomes stale. Should we auto-refresh membership?

Appendix: quick playbook script (ops notes)
1) Create canary pool: console -> infer -> create pool (name: bridge-<YYYYMMDD>-<id>)
2) Upload model variant and tag as |bridge| in model catalog
3) Configure route: add header selector X-RW-Bridge -> pool
4) Enable leash monitors in alerts panel and set paging policy
5) Kick off step1: change route percentage and start 1h timer

Notes to self / rough ideas
- Consider adding a lightweight experiment annotation that persists hypothesis, reviewers, and failure modes directly in the rollout console so canary metadata lives with traffic config.
- Prototype an "auto-cut" mechanism: when synthetic probe failures hit threshold, automatically reduce exposure by 50% and send a single notification to steward.

References and related docs (work in progress)
- See linked PR for initial implementation of Bridge headers and route filters.
- Related: rollout orchestration back-of-envelope in product backlog (ROLL-1800).

End of draft

---
Working doc style: rough, action-oriented. Will iterate with SRE and solutions before converting to canonical playbook.
